title: Shift docket — annotated checkpoints and deferred actions
content:
Context and purpose:
This file is a compact, slightly messy operator docket for the 10/11 midweek shift. Aim: capture what I observed, quick actions taken, things left to follow up, and the small runbook edits that seemed obviously needed. Not polished — notes-to-self style so next operator can pick up quickly.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Short latency spike during 02:07–02:17 UTC affecting model-router and downstream batching. Root cause likely an auto-scaler oscillation + heavy long-context requests hitting the older quantized variant.
- Immediate mitigation: scaled up dedicated pooling for model-router (manual bump), temporarily pinned traffic to model-router-v2 route for low-latency customers, evicted one problematic node from pool and cordoned it.
- Postmortem ticket started (RED-4123). Follow-ups and runbook changes below.

Active alerts at handoff (timestamps UTC):
- P99 latency alert — model-router: triggered 2026-10-11T02:08, resolved 02:22.
- Batching backlog warning — kv-cache queue depth > 80% at 02:09, auto-recover at 02:21.
- Node-restart flapping — infra-node-ax-07 restarted twice between 01:55 and 02:04. Marked cordoned.

Escalations and notes: 
- Escalated to platform-eng at 02:12 (Slack #platform-ops) because we suspected autoscaler config regression after the rollout (linked PR). Leo joined 02:15 to verify metrics and suggested pinning route.
- Customer impact: brief increased latency for Hosted API customers in EU-west. CS pinged (ticket created RED-4151) and templated note sent to impacted beta customers.

What I changed (chronological):
1) 02:09 — ran diagnostic queries (curl /metrics) against model-router instances, noticed high system CPU on ax-07 and increasing response times for warm-start tokens.
2) 02:11 — cordoned infra-node-ax-07 and drained pods; marked node for immediate post-shift deeper inspection.
3) 02:14 — manual scale +2 on model-router dedicated pool to buy headroom (command: infractl pool scale model-router dedicated 2).
4) 02:18 — updated route policy to pin critical-tier customers to model-router-v2 (temp override; rollback at 03:30). Logged change in change-log.
5) 02:24 — confirmed metrics trending back to baseline, lifted P99 alert at 02:22 and cleared backlog at 02:27.

Deferred / incomplete items (please pick up):
- Follow up with infra team to inspect ax-07 hardware logs (serial console + dmesg) — ticket created internal: RED-4160.
- Re-run the autoscaler regression test scenario in staging (scenario id: scale-surge-2026-09) and validate the hysteresis settings in autoscaler config (candidate PR referenced).
- Review and expand the runbook section for 'model-router P99 latency spike' — current doc missing explicit steps to pin routes and when to cordon nodes. I sketched edits under Confluence page svc-routing-runbooks but did not commit.

Runbook edits I think are needed (quick patch notes):
- Add a quick checklist: 
  - Check autoscaler metrics: compare desiredReplicas vs actualReplicas for last 15m.
  - If autoscaler shows oscillation AND node-level CPU spikes on a single node, cordon node first, then scale pool +1.
  - If batching backlog > 70% for >5m, temporarily reduce max-sequence-length for non-critical routes to force smaller batches.
- Add example commands and exact Slack escalation channels (to avoid hunting).
- Note: include a small snippet to detect long-context large requests by inspecting request.histogram for token_length > 2048.

Observations / anomalies (no actions yet):
- The problem appeared correlated with a burst of requests that had long contexts (many were internal eval jobs hitting hosted API with 'debug-long' marker). We should consider rate-limiting internal evaluation traffic unless it’s on dedicated capacity.
- One of the model-router instances had slightly older model weights (v1.9) and a mismatch in quantization profile; this increases token latency for long contexts. Need to confirm why rollout wasn't uniform. Likely related to canary scheduling in release-engineering.

Quick commands and checks I used (so you don't re-run expensive steps):
- infractl pool list model-router --verbose (shows per-node CPU/alloc)
- kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep model-router
- curl http://metrics.internal/services/model-router | jq '.p99,.cpu'
- autoscalerctl history model-router --last 60m

Customer comms status:
- CS ticket RED-4151 created; templated note sent to EU-hosted beta customers at 03:05. No SLA credit decision yet — hold until postmortem.

Questions for follow-up (assignable):
- Release-eng: why did a model-router node run an older artifact? See GH PR pr/9874 (might be scheduling bug).
- ML infra: should we throttle internal eval workloads hitting hosted API during peak hours? (Aria to advise.)
- Platform: confirm autoscaler hysteresis defaults and whether we rolled a change in the last week.

Notes-to-self and TODO (short):
- Add a small test case for 'long-context flood' into chaos-suite.
- Add a metric alert for 'auto-scale thrash' (pattern: desiredReplicas spikes >30% within 10m).
- Move the temporary route pin rollback into a follow-up change that’s safe to run from runbook (I rolled it manually — should make it a documented play).

Hand-off guidance for the next operator:
- If you see model-router P99 rising again, first check autoscaler desired vs actual then look for single-node CPU tail. If single-node is the culprit, cordon it first. Scaling is second.
- Do not run broad-scale restarts on the pool — that amplified instability during tests. Prefer cordon + drain.
- If batching backlog persists >10m, temporarily downgrade model variant for non-critical routes (steps in runbook draft).

Useful links and artifacts (quick reference):
- Post-incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-4123
- Customer impact ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RED-4151
- Runbook draft (do not edit final): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/svc-routing-runbooks
- Suspected PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/9874

End-of-shift status:
- Alerts cleared, main services within SLOs, node ax-07 cordoned and marked for hardware inspection. Manual route pin still active (rollback scheduled 2026-10-11T11:30Z) — please confirm rollback or escalate if metrics still abnormal.

Signed-off: Maya (oncall/operator).

-- raw scratch lines below (feel free to ignore if you pick this up) --
- Scratch: 02:05 saw one off request with token_length 9876 from user-id internal/eval-332 — tracked to eval job eval-332; pinged eval infra.
- Scratch: consider adding a temporary whitelist for internal evals to use dedicated capacity.
